# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b91 — Working DRY-only PID, restart continuity and stable dashboard

Beta91 builds directly on v0.6.0b90. All previously published physical-device safety protections, minimum ON/OFF compressor dwell, startup grace, independent upstream supply cooldown, window/sleep rules, multi-room controller permissions and configuration are retained.

## DRY-only dehumidifiers can now use safe PID pulses

- HEM recognizes that a physical dehumidifier exposing only **dry** and **off** never supports **heat** or **cool**. PID regulates measured relative humidity against the configured humidity target and only selects native supported modes.
- The older Greek status incorrectly read **"PID requests heating or cooling, but output remains off"** even for DRY devices. This was a generic `pid_output_inactive` label, **not a heating/cooling command or a failed physical acknowledgement**. The status is now correctly described as PID waiting for the next safe activation window (English/German/Greek), and ordinary PID duty-cycle OFF periods no longer display an alarming warning icon.
- Short PID duty cycles previously produced ON windows shorter than a compressor’s physical minimum ON time; the original `duty_on` rejected these every time. The new universal bounded `safe_binary_pwm_cycle` aggregates an integer number of configured PWM periods into a longer window (never more than 24 hours), allowing a complete minimum-runtime ON pulse while maintaining approximately the same long-run duty percentage. Truly negligible demand remains safely inactive.
- Native minimum ON/OFF, maximum runtime, defrost, window/sleep, verified source identity, physical ACK/retry and upstream supply interlocks are **unchanged**. Output can never be forced by a low-demand pulse if the physical device is not safe to start. No device-specific exception or false native mode is introduced.
- Existing controller diagnostics now show the exact control metric, effective PWM cycle, actual PWM phase, and next scheduled activation window, without adding error entities.

## Safe PID restart continuity

- Managed PID integral, derivative-reseed measurement and logical PWM anchor are checkpointed at bounded sample intervals in the existing HA Store, tied to the physical source identity and control settings. Restart preserves mathematical integral and PWM phase only when current independent feedback and checkpoint timestamps are verified.
- The offline period is **never** integrated into PID demand; derivative is seeded to zero to avoid a startup kick. Stale, corrupt and mismatched checkpoints are rejected. Physical ON/OFF records and supply cooldown timestamps remain separate and persist independently.
- Explicit control edits, native physical manual overrides and sleep/window holds invalidate the mathematical checkpoint but do not erase hardware dwell safety history.

## Dashboard glitching fixed

- Instead of tearing down and recreating the whole connected Lovelace card for every HA weather, room or native actuator update, Beta91 reconciles text/attributes and keyed nodes in place. This preserves expanded rooms/devices, current focus, scroll position and popups. Room ordering no longer reshuffles when warning states change.

## Verification

The release executes real source-defined controller and native actuator tests with only `dry/off` modes, safe 20% and 8% dehumidification PID pulses, no unsupported heat/cool commands, zero/unknown demand holds, minimum-ON/OFF protections, power-switch restart history, all existing Beta70–90 hardware protections, and 60 consecutive real Chromium card updates with stable DOM identity/focus/scroll/popups. All 38 translation files and the canonical HACS ZIP are verified before publishing.

## Install

Update HEM to **v0.6.0b91** through HACS prereleases, restart Home Assistant, and hard-refresh Lovelace. Existing device entities, power-switch setup, authorization and controller configuration are preserved. Real hardware behavior still depends on the physical device reporting valid native state and acknowledging its commands.
